mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns in downturns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last two quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of quarters with declining GDP, or 60-day forward returns in declining GDP periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 5-day forward returns in tight labor market periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% within the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related industries benefit from increased activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in housing market expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns in inflationary periods with tight monetary policy are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are revised upwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of quarters with increasing RSAFS, or 20-day forward returns in periods of increasing RSAFS are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
